skills_considered.reason: The XML came from this supplier session's sweep. The figures needed three routes: the PMC OA package FTP path returned 404 despite oa.fcgi advertising it, the Springer CDN refused the .jpg names the XML declares, and the working route was europepmc.org/webservices/rest/PMC10770339/supplementaryFiles for the supplements plus the Springer CDN with .png for the original-resolution figures.
Run inline. Every load-bearing finding here is a panel reading, and a read-only sub-agent cannot open a PNG at original resolution.
Two discovery-grade items land in the discovery ledger from this reading: the inverted title as a triage hazard, and simvastatin/MCM7 as a repurposing seed with its caveats attached.

Simvastatin is a repurposing seed here, not a candidate. BLOCK-1 triage would be premature: the target is MCM7 in bone, the CNS rationale for a WWOX-DEE genotype is absent, and the paper's own control cells are affected by the drug (Fig 7C) contrary to its text.

corpus_crossquery.query: Does any WWOX surface in this repository record a direction for WWOX on MYC, and does it agree with what this paper measures?
corpus_crossquery.finding: PMID 29724996, read and closed earlier today, concludes that WWOX negatively modulates c-Myc in liver. This paper measures the same direction in bone: WWOX loss raises Myc, WWOX re-expression lowers it, and human OS with low WWOX has higher MYC. There is no directional conflict in the biology. The conflict is between this paper's findings and this paper's own title.

retraction_check.result: No retraction and no expression of concern. One ORDINARY ERRATUM is attached: PMID 38355659, Cell Death Dis 2024, which corrects a single author name from 'Ameen Haji Yehya' to 'Ameen Haj-Yahia'. It corrects no datum, no figure and no conclusion. Per the corpus rule this is annotated and does NOT create a PUBLICATION_INTEGRITY_HOLD. The erratum was retrieved as a structured surface during this session's sweep and read in full; it is one page and its whole content is the name correction. It does NOT correct the title.

supplement_page_renders.why: The supplementary figures exist only inside a PDF, so a panel can be inspected only as a rendered page. The render is recorded as a reproducible recipe in the manner of page_adjudications: source digest, page, dpi and the digest of the resulting image, so a reader with their own copy regenerates identical bytes without this repository redistributing the publisher's figure.
supplement_page_renders.renderer: PyMuPDF 1.26.5 (MuPDF 1.26.10), page.get_pixmap(dpi=220), full page, no crop
supplement_page_renders.also_rendered_not_cited: S2 (page 5) and S3 (page 6) were rendered at the same settings and inspected; no locator draws on them, so their digests are not declared as evidentiary artifacts.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: PMCID PMC10770339, JATS XML served by PMC, CC BY, in the PMC open-access subset. The OA package FTP path advertised by oa.fcgi returned HTTP 404 over the HTTPS mirror. Figures were obtained at original resolution (1835-1975 px wide) from the Springer Nature static CDN as PNG; the XML declares the same figures as .jpg, and requesting .jpg yielded seven byte-identical 4 KB HTML error pages. The distinct-digest check caught that before any of them could be declared a figure. The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint additionally delivered both supplements and a 790 px display copy of each figure, which was discarded in favour of the originals.
verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: No locator is abstract-anchored. The abstract is used once, as the OBJECT of a locator rather than as its evidence: it is quoted nowhere, but its agreement with the body is the fact that isolates the title as the sole inverted surface.
verbatim_locators.panel_text_relation_note: Every entry carries panel_text_relation. The five contradictions are one-directional: the figure entry carries text_contradicted_by_panel plus contradicts: entries[N] pointing at the text locator it overturns, and that text locator is an ordinary text_only entry. The single confirmation carries text_confirmed_by_panel on the figure side. NOTE FOR THE SPEC: a pointer field is defined for contradiction but not for confirmation, so the link between a confirming panel and the sentence it confirms is currently expressed only in the propositions. No field was coined for it here. RETROFIT 2026-08-10, citation audit — the count above is now wrong and is left standing so the change is visible: FOUR pairs remained after the supplement pass, and the audit leaves TWO. Every contradicted sentence now carries the author's own figure citation inside its snippet, and every paired panel entry carries a cited_panel_check saying whether the panel it reads is the panel the sentence cites. 7C and S5F pass. 6G and 6C do not: the sentences cite 6D and 6A-B. Those two are DOWNGRADED to panel_qualifies_text with a qualifies pointer, not re-pointed — re-pointing would have made the pairs look sound and erased the mismatch, which is itself a finding. panel_qualifies_text and qualifies are coined here ahead of the spec, on the same footing as panel_text_relation before the validator required it; the pointer grammar and the needle rule are inherited unchanged. The rule the audit encodes: a pair is a contradiction only when the falsifying panel is the panel the sentence itself cites — otherwise the reader chose the panel, and a reader-chosen panel can qualify a claim but cannot make the paper contradict itself.

entries.proposition: THE HEADLINE FINDING, AND IT IS NOT BIOLOGY. The paper's own body states the direction plainly: WWOX loss RAISES Myc. This is the same direction measured in liver by PMID 29724996. There is no cross-tissue conflict.
entries.snippet: depletion of WWOX results in Myc upregulation as an early event
entries.anchor: Results, 'WWOX loss results in Myc alteration in yBM cells', closing sentence of the ChIP-Seq paragraph

entries.proposition: Panel side of the direction: the figure legend itself states the inverse correlation, and panel H shows it in human tumours. The TITLE of this paper asserts the opposite of this caption — 'WWOX promotes osteosarcoma development via upregulation of Myc' says WWOX promotes the tumour and raises MYC, when the paper shows WWOX LOSS does both. The title is the artifact that travels: it is what PubMed carries, what the NOT_EVIDENCE abstract corpus TSV carries, and what a title-level triage records. A model built from titles files WWOX as a bone oncogene.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 6 caption reads 'WWOX expression is inversely correlated with c-Myc in OS.' Panel H, TCGA TARGET GTEx box plot: High WWOX median Log2(norm_count+1) ~11.0, Low WWOX median ~11.4, P-value <0.001 printed in-plot, with the two interquartile ranges overlapping across most of their span.
entries.anchor: Figure 6, caption title and panel H, read at original resolution 1956 px wide

entries.proposition: QUALIFIED PAIR, BODY SIDE. The text calls the WWOX add-back a restoration and its effect on Myc a significant reduction, and cites Fig 6D for it. Fig 6D contains no WWOX re-expression arm at all — see entries[28] for its own caption and entries[29] for its panels — so the citation does not point at the experiment the sentence reports.
entries.snippet: significant reduction in Myc levels upon WWOX restoration (Fig. 6D )
entries.anchor: Results, 'WWOX loss results in Myc alteration in yBM cells', ChIP-Seq paragraph

entries.proposition: QUALIFIED PAIR, PANEL SIDE — DOWNGRADED FROM CONTRADICTION 2026-08-10. Fig 6G is the only panel in the article that carries a WWOX overexpression lane, so it is where the sentence's experiment actually lives; but it is NOT the panel the sentence cites, and a panel the sentence does not cite cannot be that sentence's own evidence turning against it. What it can do is qualify: the blot's quantification puts WWOX at 9x the SKO baseline while the Myc level it produces is 0.4, well BELOW the baseline of 1, so a supraphysiological dose that overshoots the reference cannot establish what physiological WWOX sets Myc to; and the panel carries no replicates and no error while the text calls the reduction significant. Both remain true. What changes is the strength of the claim: this is a qualification plus a mis-citation, not a self-falsification.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 6G lane quantifications, printed under the bands: WWOX 1 (SKO-yBM parental), 0.05 (DKO-yBM parental), 9 (DKO-yBM OE); c-Myc 1, 1.4, 0.4 across the same three lanes. No n, no error bars and no significance marks appear anywhere in the panel.
entries.anchor: Figure 6, panel G, lane quantification numbers read at original resolution
entries.qualifies_needle: reduction in Myc levels upon WWOX restoration
entries.cited_panel_check: MISMATCH. The sentence cites (Fig. 6D ); this locator reads Fig 6G. Reclassified rather than re-pointed: re-pointing would have hidden the mismatch, and the mismatch is itself the finding. FIELD COINED AHEAD OF THE SPEC: panel_qualifies_text and its pointer qualifies are emitted here for the first time, on the same basis panel_text_relation was emitted before the validator required it. The pointer grammar and the needle rule are unchanged from contradicts.

entries.proposition: QUALIFIED PAIR, BODY SIDE — AND A CORRECTION OF THIS MANIFEST'S OWN QUOTING. The text describes Myc as lowly expressed in the p53-only knockout, which is what makes the Myc programme 'unique' to the double knockout. The first version of this locator stopped the quote at 'in SKO yBM' and so removed the author's own comparator, 'as compared to those in DKO cells'. With the comparator restored the sentence is RELATIVE and it is true; clipping it made it look absolute, and the pair that rested on the clipped form was my construction rather than the paper's error. The snippet now runs to the citation the passage gives, (Fig. 6A, B ).
entries.snippet: low expression of Myc and its targets in SKO yBM as compared to those in DKO cells. In fact, the Myc target pathway was unique to yBM DKO cells (Fig. 6A, B )
entries.anchor: Results, 'WWOX loss results in Myc alteration in yBM cells', opening sentence

entries.proposition: QUALIFIED PAIR, PANEL SIDE — DOWNGRADED FROM CONTRADICTION 2026-08-10. Two reasons, and either alone is sufficient. First, the sentence cites Fig 6A, B — the Venn and the pathway bar graph — while this locator reads Fig 6C, which the NEXT sentence cites for a different proposition. Second, with the author's comparator restored the sentence claims low expression relative to DKO, which Fig 6C confirms rather than denies. What survives is a qualification, and it is worth keeping: against the true Control, SKO Myc is not low in absolute terms — it is 2.6-fold up and significant — so the double knockout adds to a programme already running rather than creating it. 'Unique to DKO' holds for the pathway-enrichment comparison against SKO, not for the level of Myc itself.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 6C, Myc panel: Control 1.0, yBM-SKO ~2.6 marked ** against Control, yBM-DKO ~4.15 marked *** against Control and * against SKO. In the adjacent Mcm7 panel the Control-to-SKO comparison is marked ns.
entries.anchor: Figure 6, panel C, Myc and Mcm7 bar charts with their significance brackets, read at original resolution
entries.qualifies_needle: low expression of Myc and its targets in SKO yBM
entries.cited_panel_check: MISMATCH. The sentence cites (Fig. 6A, B ); this locator reads Fig 6C. 6C is cited in the same paragraph, but by the following sentence and for a different assertion — proximity in a paragraph is not a citation.

Cited panel and falsifying panel are the same, so the selectivity claim is overturned by its own evidence. This is one of the two pairs in this manifest that survived the 2026-08-10 citation audit unchanged.

entries.proposition: The text reports the double knockout as roughly half-penetrant for tumour formation, against a p53-only arm that forms none. Verified against the panel it actually cites, Fig S5B: 0/13 versus 11/21 (52.4%). The sentence is accurate; it was my earlier pairing to Fig 4D that was not.

entries.anchor: Results, 'Trp53 SKO yBM is not tumorigenic', closing sentence

entries.proposition: CORRECTED AFTER READING THE SUPPLEMENT — MY EARLIER PAIRING WAS A MIS-ATTRIBUTION. The sentence cites Fig S5A,B, and against Fig S5B the phrase 'about 50%' is ACCURATE: the panel prints 11/21 (52.4%). I had paired it with Fig 4D (12/28, 42.9%) and called it an upward rounding; that was reading the text against a panel it does not cite, and it was possible only because the supplement was unread. What the two panels DO show, and what the paper never reconciles, is TWO INCOMPATIBLE COUNTS for the same genotype: 12 of 28 in the main figure and 11 of 21 in the supplement, different in both numerator and denominator.

The sentence cites Fig S4D and describes accumulation WITHIN a genotype over time, which Fig S4D does show monotonically for SKO-BM: about 9, 21 and 58 percent at 2, 4 and 8 months. The Fig 4A observation is real and kept below as its own panel_only entry, but it never contradicted this sentence.

entries.proposition: REPURPOSING SEED, recorded with its limits attached rather than promoted. Simvastatin reduced tumour size and weight in vivo and lowered MCM7 by IHC. It is a seed and not a candidate: the target is MCM7 in bone, the route to a CNS-relevant WWOX genotype is not addressed anywhere in this paper, and the in vitro selectivity claim is contradicted by the paper's own Fig 7C.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 7F: tumour size falls from ~0.42 to ~0.21 cm3 marked ****, tumour weight from ~0.71 to ~0.55 g marked ***, vehicle n~11 and simvastatin n~15 points plotted. Fig 7G: MCM7/nucleus falls from ~0.43 (4 points) to ~0.30 (6 points), marked **.

In the same figures Myc Targets V2 and V1 are the top two enriched pathways, reaching adjusted p -log10 of ~22 in Fig 5C and ~18 in Fig 5F.

entries.proposition: The Discussion states the direction as the study's own claim of clear evidence, which is what isolates the fault to the title alone: body, figure caption and abstract all say WWOX LOSS raises Myc, and only the title says WWOX raises Myc. Recorded here from the BODY. The abstract's agreeing sentence — 'Restoration of WWOX in double-knockout young BM cells reduced Myc protein levels' — is deliberately NOT quoted as a locator: it exists only in the abstract, and this manifest's first attempt did declare it as body text until the abstract/body separation refused it. That refusal is itself the reason the claim can be trusted now.
entries.snippet: our study provides clear evidence that combined deletion of WWOX and p53 resulted in increased Myc levels
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph beginning 'Remarkably, our DKO yBM cells expressed high levels of Myc in comparison to SKO-yBM cells'

entries.proposition: SUPPLEMENT PAIR, PANEL SIDE. MCM7 is NOT higher in the panel the sentence cites. Its own quantification puts the two SKO lanes at 1 and 0.8 and the three DKO lanes at 1, 1.2 and 1.2 — a spread that overlaps completely. c-Myc in the same blot does separate. The claim holds for Myc and fails for MCM7, and MCM7 is the target the therapeutic arm is built on.

verbatim_locators.note: Coverage: COMPLETE. Introduction, Materials and methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions and the reference list read in the JATS body; all seven main figures inspected as images at original resolution (1835-1975 px); the erratum PMID 38355659 read in full as a structured surface; and all five supplementary figures S1-S5 inspected as full-page renders of the source PDF at 220 dpi, with the render recipe recorded above. MOESM2, a PowerPoint of the same figures, was retrieved and not opened; it carries no content absent from MOESM1. THE SUPPLEMENT PASS WAS NOT A FORMALITY: it corrected two of this manifest's own contradiction pairs, both of which had matched a text sentence to a main figure the sentence does not cite, and it produced four findings that exist only there. That is the concrete cost of the earlier partial state, and the reason the receipt writer was right to refuse a complete read on the first pass.
